title: Optimizers: SGD to Adam
oneLine: Turn raw gradients into stable, fast parameter updates.

paras: Plain SGD takes a fixed step against the gradient. Momentum smooths the path by accumulating a velocity; Adam goes further, keeping per-parameter running averages of the gradient and its square so each weight gets its own adaptive step size. Adam is the default for most deep learning.
Adam rescales each step by a running estimate of the gradient and its magnitude:
sections.texNote: m is the momentum (first moment), v the per-parameter scale (second moment).

sections.code:
m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g
v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g*g
mh, vh = m/(1-beta1**t), v/(1-beta2**t)
theta -= lr * mh / (np.sqrt(vh) + 1e-8)
sections.caption: Momentum plus per-parameter scaling - the Adam update.

takeaways: Momentum smooths noisy gradients into a steadier path.
Adam gives each parameter its own adaptive step size.
It is the safe default for most deep networks.
